title: Data Security
learning_outcomes: Explain data security and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of data security to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study data security in the context of ethics, privacy, and professional practice. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Data Security matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: Visual overview: Data Security
content_blocks.alt_text: Lesson 250: Data Security; a three-stage visual for understanding the topic, applying it to a small example, and validating assumptions.
content_blocks.caption: Use the overview to connect data security to a concrete example and a responsible check.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Responsible data science considers the whole lifecycle: consent and legal basis, minimization, privacy, fairness, security, explainability, human oversight, and a path to challenge or correct decisions.

items.title: Access control
items.text: Define access control in relation to data security; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

items.title: Credential management
items.text: Work through credential management using a small, synthetic example before scaling up. State what the calculation or method returns and why that result is useful.

items.title: Encryption concepts
items.text: Check the edge cases for encryption concepts: missing values, unusual ranges, different groups, time boundaries, or a changed input can affect the conclusion.

items.title: Secure data storage
items.text: Document the rule or choice for secure data storage so another learner can reproduce the analysis and understand its limitations.

items.title: Handling confidential datasets
items.text: Define handling confidential datasets in relation to data security; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by data security. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. Responsible communication records assumptions, limitations, and a concrete path to improve the evidence.

content_blocks.title: Responsible interpretation
content_blocks.text: This example is a teaching aid. It is static in the CodeLeaf lesson and is not executed in the browser. It uses small synthetic values; validate any real workflow in a separate, appropriate local environment and protect sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Responsible data science considers the whole lifecycle: consent and legal basis, minimization, privacy, fairness, security, explainability, human oversight, and a path to challenge or correct decisions. Next, connect this lesson to the linked prerequisite or following lesson. Record the method, input assumptions, observed result, and one limitation so another person can reproduce and review the work.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small synthetic example for data security. State a question, make a prediction, trace or run an appropriate calculation, then write one finding and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: Refer accurately to the topic and its syllabus subtopics.
Record a reproducible example or a complete manual trace with an expected result.
Document at least one assumption, limitation, data-quality issue, or evaluation check.
hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
troubleshooting: Check input values, path assumptions, package versions, indentation, and units.
For SQL, use a local schema and read-only test data; this page does not provide a live database.
For package-dependent work, create an isolated environment and use the relevant official documentation.
